phrases.text: Napoleon has gathered more than six hundred thousand men, the largest army Europe has ever seen.
In June, they cross the Niemen River, into Russia.
But the Russians refuse to fight. They retreat east, burning what they leave behind.
In September, at Borodino, the two armies finally collide, in one of the bloodiest single days of the age.
A week later, Napoleon marches into Moscow. The city is almost empty, and within hours, it's on fire.
He waits for a surrender that never comes. In October, he turns back.
Of the hundreds of thousands who set out, only a fraction ever made it home.
